findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition - older 4-argument signature is unreachable
findings.body: Two class methods named `self.downsize` are now defined on OptimizedImage (lines 145-147 and 149-151). Ruby does not support method overloading: redefining a method silently replaces the previous one, so the older `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` becomes dead code and the only `downsize` that actually exists is `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Any other caller in the codebase that still uses the old signature with separate integer width/height arguments will be dispatched to the new method, where the third positional argument is interpreted as a single `dimensions` string. For example, `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)` would set `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200` (an Integer), and any subsequent use of `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` or `opts[:allow_animation]` will raise a `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` because `Integer` does not respond to `[]`. Either remove one of the two definitions, or rename the new method (e.g., `downsize_to_dimensions` / `downsize_to`) so both signatures remain callable.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value, wasting 5 attempts on failure
findings.body: The new downsize loop in `create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` but does not inspect its return value. `OptimizedImage.downsize` swallows all exceptions internally and returns `false` on failure (ImageMagick/gifsicle errors, corrupt or unsupported image, missing binary, etc.), so when downsize fails the on-disk size does not decrease and the loop spins through all 5 attempts pointlessly, each time re-invoking ImageMagick on a file it cannot process. After exiting, the still-too-large file is handed to `Upload.create_for`, which will reject it and surface a confusing error to the user after several wasted conversions. The call should be checked (break out of the loop and ideally abort the upload on `false`) or wrapped in a rescue that bails out of the downsize attempt early.
